extracted.intended_audience: users of Singular (mathematicians / researchers doing polynomial computations in commutative algebra, algebraic geometry, and singularity theory)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical manual and reference for using the Singular computer algebra system: how to run it interactively or under Emacs, define rings and variables, write procedures and libraries, compute Groebner/standard bases, modules/resolutions, and use the built-in help and options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command termination
rubrics_metrics.description: Every command has to be terminated by a ; (semicolon) followed by RETURN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The semicolon is required to end statements. The semicolon is not interpreted as end-of-command if it occurs inside a string. Singular waits for blocks (curly braces) and open quotes to be closed before accepting input. Additional semicolons are allowed and are treated as empty statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive prompt meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: The prompt > asks the user for input; the continuation prompt . indicates input of missing parts of a command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you see the dot prompt after typing a line it means input is incomplete (e.g., missing semicolon, closing } or ").

rubrics_metrics.name: Entering and exiting Singular / ESingular
rubrics_metrics.description: Start Singular via Singular (ASCII terminal) or ESingular / M-x singular (Emacs). Exit with quit;, exit;, or $ (or C-c $ in Emacs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emacs interface is recommended for convenience and extra features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: All input in Singular is case sensitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Names, commands, variables, and library/procedure names are case sensitive — choose consistent capitalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Object types and assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Every object has a type (e.g., int for integers). Assignments use =. Equality and inequality tests use == and != (or <>).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 0 represents FALSE; any non-zero value represents TRUE. Example: int k = 2; k == 2; -> 1

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Text starting with // denotes a comment and is ignored in calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use // for inline comments and to explain code snippets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strings and execute
rubrics_metrics.description: Strings are delimited by double quotes ". Strings may contain valid Singular commands and can be executed by the function execute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strings can be concatenated with +. Executing string content runs it as if typed on the command line; useful to generate rings or commands inside procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: History navigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular maintains a history of previous input lines accessible by CTRL-P (previous), CTRL-N (next), or arrow keys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use history navigation to retrieve and edit prior commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rings are required for polynomial computations
rubrics_metrics.description: To compute with ideals, modules, polynomial vectors, etc., a basering must be defined first; the basering is a polynomial ring or localization/quotient thereof over a field or some rings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple integer and string computations can be done without a ring, but most powerful computations require defining a ring. Use ring r = 0,(x,y,z),dp; to declare a polynomial ring (0 for rationals) and the monomial ordering (dp here).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ring declaration structure
rubrics_metrics.description: A ring declaration consists of three parts: ground field/coefficient ring, names of the ring variables, and the monomial ordering to be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: ring r1=32003,(x,y,z),dp; ring r3=7,(x(1..10)),ds; ring r4=(0,a),(mu,nu),lp; — use appropriate characteristic, variable naming, and ordering for your computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monomial ordering affects computations
rubrics_metrics.description: The monomial ordering directly affects the standard basis (Groebner) computations and thus algorithmic results (e.g., global vs local Milnor numbers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use local vs global orderings to test for singularities outside the origin; e.g., switching to a local ordering can change the Milnor number computed for a polynomial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Switching and fetching objects between rings
rubrics_metrics.description: When working across rings, use setring to change the active basering and fetch/imap/maps to transfer objects between rings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: fetch(r,f) efficiently fetches polynomial f from ring r; imap is more general but less efficient; maps are most general. Use fetch when possible for performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming and shorthand notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Short-hand monomial notation (e.g., x3 for x^3) is allowed but forbidden if variable names consist of more than one character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer explicit exponent notation x^3 for multi-character variable names. See Section 6.4 for details on oddities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computing standard/Groebner bases
rubrics_metrics.description: Use groebner (or groebner(...) naming) to compute a standard/Groebner basis; many related functions (reduce, kbase, vdim) operate on or with standard bases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: groebner prints a protocol during calculation when option(prot) is enabled; use option(noprot) to turn it off. To obtain a reduced standard basis use option(redSB). Example: ideal sI = groebner(f); reduce(g,sI);

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol and option controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular prints calculation protocols depending on options; option(prot) enables protocolling, option(noprot) disables it; option(redSB) requests reduced standard bases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use options to control verbosity and algorithm variants; option settings can affect algorithms and printed output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Size semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: For polynomials, size returns the number of monomials; for other objects it returns number of entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use size(f) to get monomial count; use size on other objects to inspect length/size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jacobian, kbase and vdim for Milnor numbers / quotient spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Use jacob to compute the Jacobian ideal, groebner to get a standard basis, and kbase or vdim to obtain a basis or the vector space dimension of quotient rings (e.g., Milnor number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example workflow: J = jacob(f); J = groebner(J); ideal K = kbase(J); size(K); or directly vdim(groebner(jacob(f)));

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures: defining and returning values
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures are defined with proc name(parameter_list) { ... } and may return a value with return. The parameter list specifies expected argument types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When defining a procedure, the prompt becomes '.' until the block is closed. Example: proc Milnor(poly h) { return(vdim(groebner(jacob(h)))); }

rubrics_metrics.name: Libraries: loading and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular ships libraries (collections of procedures). Load with LIB "name.lib"; list currently loaded libraries with listvar(package); and use help <symbol> or example <symbol> to see docs and examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library procedures have help parts displayed by help procname; and runnable examples via example procname; Use LIB to load libraries (e.g., LIB "sing.lib";).

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrices and modules interchangeability
rubrics_metrics.description: Matrices and modules may be interchanged; modules can be represented as (sparse) matrices in Singular and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: freemodule(n) creates a free module; module MD = [..],[..]; matrix MM = MD; syz(MD) computes relations; use quotient(U,freemodule(nrows(U))) to compute annihilator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Syzygies and resolutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use syz to compute syzygies; res(...,n) to compute free resolutions heuristically up to length n; minres to minimize a resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspection and printing of resolutions: resolution rs = res(I,0); print(betti(rs),"betti"); rs = minres(rs); print(rs[3]); — results may not be minimal until minres is applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographical conventions in the manual
rubrics_metrics.description: Typewriter font denotes Singular input/output and reserved names; the arrow → denotes Singular output; square brackets denote optional syntax; keys are shown in typewriter (e.g., N, RETURN, CTRL-P).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these conventions when reading examples; they indicate how to type commands and interpret outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help system configuration and browsers
rubrics_metrics.description: The help system is invoked by help (or ?) and can display help via various browsers (html, builtin, emacs, xinfo, lynx, etc.). The browser can be set via --browser=<browser> or system("--browser", "<browser>").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The .singularrc file can set default browser preferences. If no local HTML pages are available and --allow-net is set, the manual may be fetched from http://www.singular.uni-kl.de/Manual. Troubleshooting notes: DISPLAY must be set for X11 browsers; necessary external programs must be installed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol/verbosity control for library loading and commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Loading libraries and some commands may print additional information; use option(noprot) to disable protocol output when desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When LIB "sing.lib"; prints loading information, you can suppress or enable protocol output globally via option(prot)/option(noprot).
